questions.question: Examine the role of police, prosecution, judiciary, and correctional departments in the Indian criminal justice system
questions.solution_html:
• The criminal justice system in India consists of four major components: police
  • prosecution, judiciary, and correctional institutions.
  • Police
  • The police are responsible for maintaining law and order, preventing crime, investigating
  • offences, arresting accused persons, collecting evidence, and filing charge sheets before
  • the court.
  • Prosecution
  • The prosecution represents the State in criminal cases. Prosecutors conduct trials, present
  • evidence, examine witnesses, and ensure that justice is delivered fairly.
  • Judiciary
  • The judiciary interprets laws and delivers justice. Courts conduct fair trials, determine
  • guilt or innocence, and impose punishments according to law. The judiciary also
  • safeguards constitutional rights.
  • Correctional Departments
  • Correctional institutions such as prisons, probation, and parole systems focus on
  • reforming offenders. Their objective is rehabilitation and reintegration of offenders into
  • society.

questions.question: Read the following case study and answer the questions that follow: "A defendant is charged with a serious offense and is tried in a regular trial. The prosecution presents its case, and the defense counsel cross- examines the witnesses. The judge delivers a judgment in abridged form under Section 355 of the Cr PC." Analyze the implications of this case on the concepts of summary trials, judgments in abridged forms, and the roles of the prosecutor and defense counsel.
questions.solution_html:
• Explanation of Summary Trials and Their Scope (2 Marks)
  • Summary trials (Sections 260-265, CrPC) are used for minor offenses where the
  • procedure is simplified to speed up the process.
  • Abridged Judgments under Section 355 of the CrPC (4 Marks)
  • Section 355 of the CrPC allows a judge to deliver an abridged judgment in summary
  • trials. This provision is typically used to shorten the judgment delivery in cases where the
  • evidence is clear and the case is not complex.
  • Role of the Prosecutor (2 Marks)
  • The prosecution is responsible for presenting evidence and making the case against the
  • defendant. In a regular trial, the prosecution has to prove the guilt of the defendant
  • beyond a reasonable doubt.
  • Role of the Defense Counsel (2 Marks)
  • The defense counsel’s role is to challenge the prosecution's evidence, cross-examine
  • witnesses, and provide a defense for the defendant.
questions.final_answer: witnesses, and provide a defense for the defendant.
